rules.text: If the horizontal positions encode progression through the displayed reporting period from left to right, the vertical axis labeled "Count" is encoded by its printed tick values despite their increase downward on the page, and the route whose label names rising-case escalation is the pathway for an increasing reported-case trajectory, then a line moving from near the 0 tick at the left toward values beyond the 1400 tick at the right supports that escalation route.
rules.conditions: The printed Count-axis inscriptions accurately define the vertical value direction; the plotted series represents reported case activity; and the route label's rising-case wording is the applicable task-to-action relation.

rules.text: If the unusual downward increase of the printed Count tick values is not accepted as the chart's operative quantitative encoding, the line's downward screen-space direction alone does not establish whether reported case counts rose or fell; a routing decision based on trajectory is therefore not supported until that encoding is checked.
rules.conditions: This applies because screen-space direction is not itself a validated mapping to the measured quantity, and no legend or annotation visibly explains the inverted-looking vertical orientation.

observations.content: The chart title visibly reads "Month vs. Number of cases," and the vertical-axis label visibly reads "Count."
The visible Count-axis inscriptions place "0" near the top and then "200," "400," "600," "800," "1000," "1200," and "1400" at successively lower page positions.

observations.location: blue plotted series from left edge to right edge
observations.content: The leftmost blue marker is near the horizontal level of the printed 0 tick, while the rightmost blue marker is lower on the page than the printed 1400 tick; the connected blue line generally moves downward across the page.

chains.claim: The support for an increasing case trajectory depends on accepting the downward-increasing Count-axis inscriptions as the operative scale; the line's visible downward direction alone permits an opposite geometric reading and leaves an encoding-check support gap.

added_observations.location: x-axis date-label area beneath the plotted markers
added_observations.content: Despite substantial overlap among the angled date inscriptions, the rightmost visible label reads "Mar 22, 2020," the adjacent labels to its left show earlier March dates, and the visible March day numbers generally progress toward later dates from left to right.

refinements.condition_note: The horizontal chronology premise is visibly supported by the generally left-to-right progression of the overlapping March date inscriptions, provided those inscriptions are the x-axis labels associated with the plotted markers; the overlap prevents unambiguous marker-by-marker label attachment.
refinements.reason: This supplies direct visible support for the left-to-right reporting-period condition in the existing rising-trajectory chain while preserving the qualification caused by label overlap.
